3º de Primaria · Inglés · Tema 7

Wild animals

Nombre: ______________________   Fecha: ___________

Qué vas a aprender

  • Name wild animals and where they live
  • Describe animals with adjectives: big, small, fast, slow, dangerous
  • Use It's got and It can to describe an animal
  • Read and write a short animal fact file
  • Name animals of the desert and the ocean
  • Compare animals with bigger, faster and taller than
  • Name animal homes and animal babies
  • Understand why some animals are in danger and how we can help

Para pensar

Tu perro y un lobo se parecen mucho. Pero uno vive contigo y el otro, en el bosque. ¿Cómo se dice en inglés esa diferencia?

Explicación

1. Pets, farm animals and wild animals

There are three groups of animals. Pets live with people at home: dogs, cats, hamsters, fish. Farm animals live on a farm: cows, pigs, sheep, hens. Wild animals live free in nature: lions, tigers, wolves, bears.

En castellano: wild significa «salvaje». Los animales salvajes no se deben tocar ni alimentar: pueden ser peligrosos y necesitan vivir libres. Por eso los vemos en la naturaleza, en documentales o en centros de protección.

2. Animals of the savannah

The savannah is a hot, dry grassland in Africa. There live the lion (león), the giraffe (jirafa), the elephant (elefante), the zebra (cebra), the hippo (hipopótamo), the rhino (rinoceronte) and the cheetah (guepardo).

The lion is the «king of the savannah». The giraffe is the tallest animal in the world. The elephant is the biggest land animal. Truco: hippo y rhino son formas cortas de hippopotamus y rhinoceros.

3. Desert animals

A desert (desierto) is a very dry place with very little rain. Some deserts are very hot in the day and cold at night. The biggest hot desert in the world is the Sahara, in Africa.

Animals in the desert are special: they can live with very little water.

  • The camel (camello) has got one or two humps (jorobas). It stores fat in them. It can walk for days without water!
  • The fennec fox (fénec) is a small fox with very big ears. Its ears help it lose heat and hear small animals under the sand.
  • The scorpion (escorpión) has got eight legs and a tail with a sting (aguijón).
  • The lizard (lagarto) and the snake hide under rocks when it's very hot.
  • The meerkat (suricata) lives in groups and stands on its back legs to look for danger.

Many desert animals sleep in the day and go out at night, when it's cooler.

Activity: choose a desert animal and write three sentences: «It's got… It can… It eats…».

4. Animals of the jungle

The jungle or rainforest is hot and wet, with lots of trees. There live the monkey (mono), the parrot (loro), the snake (serpiente), the tiger (tigre), the gorilla, the frog (rana) and the crocodile (cocodrilo), in the rivers.

Monkeys swing from tree to tree. Parrots are very colourful and some can repeat words. Some frogs are tiny but poisonous! ¿Sabes qué animal de la selva tiene rayas negras y naranjas? ¡El tiger!

5. Cold places: polar animals

In very cold places, like the Arctic and the Antarctic, there are animals with thick fur or fat. The polar bear (oso polar) lives in the Arctic. Penguins (pingüinos) live in the Antarctic. There are also seals (focas), walruses (morsas) and arctic foxes (zorros árticos).

In the ocean live the whale (ballena), the biggest animal in the world, the dolphin (delfín), the shark (tiburón) and the octopus (pulpo), which has got eight arms.

6. Ocean animals

The ocean (océano) covers most of our planet. Millions of animals live in it.

  • The blue whale (ballena azul) is the biggest animal in the world. It's bigger than a bus! But it eats very small animals called krill.
  • The shark (tiburón) has got lots of sharp teeth. It can swim very fast.
  • The octopus (pulpo) has got eight arms. It can change colour and squirt ink (echar tinta).
  • The jellyfish (medusa) hasn't got a brain or bones. Be careful: it can sting!
  • The sea turtle (tortuga marina) has got a hard shell. It lays its eggs on the beach.
  • The seahorse (caballito de mar) is a fish. The dad carries the babies!
  • The starfish (estrella de mar) usually has got five arms.

Remember: whales and dolphins are not fish. They are mammals (mamíferos): they breathe air and feed their babies with milk.

Activity: draw an ocean picture with five animals and label them in English.

7. Describing animals: adjectives

We describe animals with adjectives: big / small, tall (alto) / short, fast (rápido) / slow (lento), strong (fuerte), dangerous (peligroso), beautiful, funny (gracioso) and scary (que da miedo).

The adjective goes before the noun or after is: «It's a big animal» / «The elephant is big». Adjectives never take -s: «two big elephants», not «bigs». Opuestos: big-small, fast-slow, tall-short.

8. Bigger, faster, taller

To compare (comparar) two animals, we add -er to the adjective and use than (que):

  • fast → faster: «A cheetah is faster than a lion.»
  • tall → taller: «A giraffe is taller than an elephant.»
  • small → smaller: «A mouse is smaller than a cat.»
  • long → longer: «A snake is longer than a worm.»

Some adjectives change a little:

  • big → bigger (double g): «An elephant is bigger than a horse.»
  • heavy → heavier (y → i): «A hippo is heavier than a zebra.»
  • funny → funnier: «A monkey is funnier than a snail.»

And there are irregular ones: good → better, bad → worse.

Game: Compare! The teacher says two animals and an adjective: «A tortoise and a rabbit… fast!» You say: «A rabbit is faster than a tortoise.»

Activity: write five sentences comparing animals.

9. It's got… It can…

To describe an animal, we say what it has got and what it can do. «The giraffe has got a long neck and long legs. It can eat leaves from tall trees.» «The crocodile has got big teeth. It can swim, but it can't climb.»

Body parts of animals: trunk (trompa), tail (cola), wings (alas), fur (pelaje), stripes (rayas), spots (manchas), horn (cuerno), claws (garras) and beak (pico). «A zebra has got black and white stripes.»

10. What do they eat?

Some animals eat meat (carne): lions, tigers, sharks and crocodiles. They are carnivores. Other animals eat plants: elephants, giraffes, zebras and rabbits. They are herbivores. Some animals eat everything, like bears and monkeys: they are omnivores.

Say it in English: «Lions eat meat.» «Giraffes eat leaves.» «Monkeys eat fruit and insects.» Estas palabras son casi iguales en castellano: carnívoro, herbívoro, omnívoro.

11. Animal homes

Animals need a home (hogar) to sleep, hide and look after their babies. Each animal has got a different kind of home:

  • A bird lives in a nest (nido).
  • A rabbit lives in a burrow (madriguera) under the ground.
  • A bee lives in a hive (colmena).
  • A spider lives on a web (tela de araña).
  • A fox and a wolf live in a den (guarida).
  • A bat lives in a cave (cueva).
  • A snail carries its home on its back: a shell (concha).
  • An ant lives in an anthill (hormiguero) with thousands of other ants.

Some animals build their homes: birds use small sticks, leaves and mud (barro); bees make wax (cera); spiders make silk (seda).

To ask: «Where does a bee live?» – «It lives in a hive.»

Remember: we must never break a nest or touch the eggs. The parents can leave them.

Activity: draw four animals and their homes and write a sentence for each one.

12. Reading: my animal fact file

Read Lucas's fact file (ficha de datos): «Animal: the elephant. Where does it live? In the savannah and in the jungle in Africa and Asia. What does it look like? It's very big and grey. It's got big ears, a long trunk and two white tusks (colmillos). What can it do? It can swim and it can carry heavy things with its trunk. It can't jump. What does it eat? Grass, leaves and fruit. Fun fact: elephants can live for 70 years!»

Answer: What colour is the elephant? Can it jump?

13. Animals in danger

Some animals are in danger (en peligro): there are very few of them, and they can disappear forever (desaparecer para siempre). We say these animals are endangered.

Why are they in danger?

  • People cut down forests (talar bosques), so the animals lose their homes.
  • There is pollution (contaminación) in the sea, rivers and air. Plastic in the sea hurts turtles and fish.
  • People hunt (cazar) some animals.
  • The planet is getting hotter: in the Arctic the ice melts (se derrite), and polar bears can't find food.

Animals in danger: the orangutan, the tiger, some sea turtles, the gorilla… And in Spain, the Iberian lynx was in great danger, but now there are more!

How can we help?

  • Don't throw rubbish (basura) on the ground or in the sea.
  • Use less plastic and recycle.
  • Respect animals in nature: don't touch or feed them.
  • Learn about animals and tell other people.

Activity: make a poster «Help the animals!» with four tips.

14. Let's practise: guess the animal

Play Guess the animal. Think of a wild animal. Your partner asks yes/no questions: «Is it big?» — «Yes, it is.» «Has it got stripes?» — «No, it hasn't.» «Can it swim?» — «Yes, it can.» «Does it live in the jungle?» — «No, it doesn't.» «Is it a hippo?» — «Yes!»

Then write your own fact file about your favourite wild animal and draw it. Hang it on the class zoo wall (mural de la clase).

15. Animal babies

Many animal babies have got a special name in English:

  • lion, tiger, bear → cub (cachorro)
  • elephant, giraffe, whale → calf (cría)
  • kangaroo → joey
  • bird, chicken → chick (polluelo)
  • duck → duckling (patito)
  • dog → puppy (cachorrito)
  • cat → kitten (gatito)
  • frog → tadpole (renacuajo)

Some animals are born from eggs (huevos): birds, most fish, snakes, turtles and frogs. Other animals are born from their mother's body and drink their mother's milk: they are mammals, like lions, whales and people.

The kangaroo is special: the joey is very, very small when it is born. It lives in its mother's pouch (bolsa) for months.

Look at the frog: the baby doesn't look like its mum! A tadpole lives in the water and has got a tail. Then it grows legs and becomes a frog.

Activity: play memory with cards: an animal and its baby.

Wild animals

Ejercicios

  1. Traduce: león, mono, serpiente, cocodrilo.

  2. Escribe dos animales de la sabana.

  3. Escribe dos animales polares.

  4. ¿Qué significa wild?

  5. Escribe el contrario: fast, big, tall.

  6. Completa: «The elephant has got a long ___.» (trompa)

  7. Completa: «Lions eat ___.»

  8. ¿Qué es un herbivore?

  9. Pregunta si el animal sabe nadar.

  10. Escribe dos frases sobre tu animal salvaje favorito.

  11. How do you say «desierto» in English?

  12. How many arms has an octopus got?

  13. Where does a bird live?

  14. What is a lion baby called?

  15. In the reading, what does Lola eat?

  16. Complete: big → ___; heavy → ___

  17. Compare: a mouse and an elephant (small).

  18. Why can a camel live in the desert?

  19. Translate: El tiburón tiene muchos dientes afilados.

  20. Is a whale a fish? Why?

  21. Why was the Iberian lynx in danger?

  22. Write four tips to help animals in danger.

  23. Write a fact file about an ocean animal: looks, abilities, food and home.

  24. Write five sentences comparing animals with -er than.

Practica

  1. A lion is a…

    1. A) pet
    2. B) wild animal
    3. C) farm animal

  2. «Jirafa» is…

    1. A) giraffe
    2. B) zebra
    3. C) gorilla

  3. Monkeys and parrots live in the…

    1. A) Antarctic
    2. B) desert
    3. C) jungle

  4. The biggest animal in the world is the…

    1. A) elephant
    2. B) lion
    3. C) whale

  5. The opposite of fast is…

    1. A) slow
    2. B) big
    3. C) tall

  6. A zebra has got…

    1. A) wings
    2. B) stripes
    3. C) a trunk

  7. The giraffe ___ got a long neck.

    1. A) has
    2. B) have
    3. C) is

  8. Carnivores eat…

    1. A) leaves
    2. B) grass
    3. C) meat

  9. Penguins live in…

    1. A) the jungle
    2. B) the Antarctic
    3. C) the savannah

  10. «It's a ___ animal.»

    1. A) bigs
    2. B) big
    3. C) animal big

  11. The biggest animal in the world is the…

    1. A) elephant
    2. B) blue whale
    3. C) shark

  12. «A cheetah is ___ than a lion.»

    1. A) more fast
    2. B) fastest
    3. C) faster

  13. A rabbit lives in a…

    1. A) hive
    2. B) burrow
    3. C) web

  14. A kangaroo baby is a…

    1. A) joey
    2. B) calf
    3. C) puppy

  15. «Contaminación» in English is…

    1. A) rubbish
    2. B) danger
    3. C) pollution

Explícalo con tus palabras

Incluye: Qué diferencia hay entre pets, farm animals y wild animals; Qué animales viven en la sabana, la selva y los polos; Cómo describo un animal con adjetivos, has got y can; Qué comen los carnívoros y los herbívoros.

Tarjetas de repaso

Recórtalas: pregunta delante, respuesta detrás.

wild animalAnimal salvaje.
savannahSabana: lion, giraffe, zebra.
jungleSelva: monkey, parrot, snake.
polar bear / penguinOso polar / pingüino.
fast / slowRápido / lento.
dangerousPeligroso.
stripes / spotsRayas / manchas.
carnivore / herbivoreCome carne / come plantas.
Desert and oceancamel, fennec fox, scorpion; blue whale, octopus, shark, turtle.
Comparefaster than, taller than, bigger than, heavier than.
Homesnest, burrow, hive, web, den, cave, shell.
Babiescub, calf, joey, chick, puppy, kitten, tadpole.

Soluciones

  1. B) Salvaje.
  2. A) Giraffe.
  3. C) Jungle.
  4. C) La ballena azul.
  5. A) Slow.
  6. B) Rayas.
  7. A) It → has.
  8. C) Carne.
  9. B) Antártida.
  10. B) Adjetivo delante, sin -s.
  11. B) Ocean.
  12. C) Compare.
  13. B) Homes.
  14. A) Babies.
  15. C) Danger.
